sections.title: Vegetable irrigation: soil, roots and weather
sections.text: Reviewed summary of UC Small Farms Network guidance. Irrigation timing depends on soil properties, weather, crop size and rooting depth. Sandy soils generally need more frequent watering than finer soils. Heat, wind and sunshine increase drying. Evaluate moisture in the crop root zone and consider recent irrigation and weather rather than using a fixed calendar alone. Root depth varies with crop, variety, soil profile and establishment method. This guidance does not convert river discharge into a field irrigation allocation.
